entries.contamination_note: Both binary_search_tree_test.cpp (the reference grader) and its canonical inputs are public (Aider's polyglot-benchmark, itself built from Exercism's public problem-specifications). A pass on the reference grader carries no information about memorisation by itself; the hidden variant (test_bst_hidden.py, fresh values and orders computed in kit/reference/hidden/bst_hidden_test.cpp) is what discriminates: a reference pass with a hidden fail is the signal a model solved the public shape without the general one, and a pass on both carries no information about memorisation either way.

Both forth.spec.js (the reference grader, run through the kit's shim under node's built-in test runner, not Jest) and its canonical inputs are public. A pass on the reference grader carries no information about memorisation by itself; the hidden variant (test_forth_hidden.py, fresh programs in kit/reference/hidden/forth_hidden.test.mjs) is what discriminates: a reference pass with a hidden fail is the signal a model solved the public shape without the general one, and a pass on both carries no information about memorisation either way. See also the SOURCES.md note that the reference grader's assertion count is Exercism's own default (one enabled `test`, the rest `xtest`), not Aider's own preprocessed count.
